chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ali ibn 'Atiyyah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'We buy food from the ships, then we measure it, and it increases.' He said to me: 'And perhaps it decreases for you.' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'If it decreases, they return it to you.' I said: 'No.' He said: 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying food by measurement from ships when the quantity varies?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on *bay' al-madmun* (sale of guaranteed/undelivered goods) regarding food purchased from ships by volume. He establishes that the variance in quantity—whether an increase or decrease after the initial measurement—is borne by the buyer, as the transaction is based on the measured amount at the time of sale rather than the exact weight upon delivery. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility in commercial transactions where minor discrepancies in bulk goods are considered acceptable losses or gains for the buyer.
